$comment: An example nudge.json. Copy it to nudge.json and keep what you need; `nudge doctor` checks it. Keys named $comment are ignored.

assistants.$comment: name is URL-safe and picks the assistant in -a and /v1/a/<name>. database is relative to this file (default data/<name>.sqlite). Without a model, Anthropic's claude-sonnet-5 is used; it reads ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.
assistants.name: robin
assistants.instructions: Answer in the language you are written to. Keep answers short.

budget.$comment: Monthly limits on model spend in USD. Past perPlayerUsd a player's messages are refused; past monthlyUsd nothing goes to the model until the month ends. warnAt is the share at which people are told. `nudge usage` shows the spend.

extensions.$comment: from is a file or package directory relative to this file, or an installed package name. settings are checked against the extension's own schema. rooms lists the kinds of room it is on in by default (lobby, personal, shared; default all); people can turn it on or off per room with /extensions. Set enabled to false to keep an entry without installing it.

Notifications of answers and approvals, to browsers through Web Push. preview: "room" (the default) names only the room; "text" adds the start of the message. subject: how push services reach you, a mailto: or https: address. For the apps add "apns": { "keyFile", "keyId", "teamId", "bundleId" } and "fcm": { "serviceAccountFile" }; key files are read from the directory nudge runs in, or give absolute paths.
Optional: names the built-in lists don't have, such as relatives'.
Receipts and other documents per room: uploaded on the room's Documents page, text read on the host, files stored encrypted.
Shared lists per room (shopping, packing), for the model and on the room's Lists page.
Scripts: the assistant saves small programs for lookups it repeats and runs them again by name, or from a watch, without a model run. Scripts can only call tools that read.

Watches: the assistant checks something on a schedule with its tools and tells the room only what is new. Each check is a model run, so minMinutes caps how often; a watch that runs a saved script costs none, and minScriptMinutes caps that.

Triggers: a secret web address per room that Home Assistant, Uptime Kuma, GitHub or a phone Shortcut POST to, and the assistant acts on what came. url is the address senders reach this server at. Each call is a paid model run, so maxPerHour caps how often one trigger answers.

Places: reminders when you get somewhere, and addresses and routes from the server's own map (an owner picks its region under the server's Maps settings in the apps). The model sees places as ⟦PLACE:home⟧, never addresses or coordinates.

Coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot, pi, opencode) through ACC: on this machine with nothing set up, and on other machines over SSH. The assistant logs in with a key of its own; acc_hosts gives the line for ~/.ssh/authorized_keys. Needs ACC's binding (pnpm acc:fetch); off here so the example works without it.

Projects: the assistant takes a software project from idea to merged code, supervising coding agents on an exe.dev VM per project that the Nudge app on your phone launches. Needs ./extensions/acc; off here so the example works without it.

Talk to assistants on other servers once both sides' admins link them (link_assistant). Each thread runs in the background for a few rounds; a linked assistant speaks here as a guest in a room of its own and can use only what offer turns on there. Needs ./extensions/federation with its server address; off here so the example works without it.

Talk with other AI agents over the A2A protocol, without federation. Agents an admin lets in (POST /ext/a2a/clients, or the web settings) call this assistant with their token, each as a guest in a room of its own where only offer is on; the Agent Card is at /v1/a/<assistant>/ext/a2a/.well-known/agent-card.json. The assistant messages agents an admin added with message_agent. server is the address other agents reach this one at; off here so the example works without it.
Web search through your own SearXNG (JSON output on), and reading a page as text.
Talk to the assistant from Telegram. The bot token comes from TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN; people link with /link <code from nudge pair>. Off here (enabled: false) so the example works without a token.
Talk to the assistant from Signal through `signal-cli -a <number> daemon --tcp --receive-mode=on-connection` on this host.
Talk to the assistant from Matrix rooms without end-to-end encryption, as a bot account whose access token is in MATRIX_ACCESS_TOKEN.

assistants.$comment: A second assistant with its own database, on the local server below. Its rooms, players and memory are separate from robin's.
assistants.name: pocket

privacy.$comment: Off by default: only secrets, ID, card and account numbers, e-mail addresses, phone numbers and what people make private are hidden (ADR 15). deep: "required" also hides names, places and organisations with a local model (about 260 MB, into server/models) and refuses requests until it runs, "preferred" sends them with the rules alone meanwhile. allow lists words it should never hide, such as a shop it takes for a person.

providers.$comment: Any OpenAI-compatible server, such as llama-server, Ollama or vLLM. apiKeyEnv names the environment variable holding its key; leave it out for keyless servers. Most local servers reject the developer role.

backup.$comment: Encrypted backups nudge serve makes on its own: everything needed to restore, into dir (relative to this file). The key is NUDGE_BACKUP_KEY or nudge-backup.key beside this file; keep a copy of it off the machine. nudge backup makes one now, nudge restore <file> --to <dir> unpacks one. "remote": { "type": "s3", "endpoint", "bucket", "region"?, "prefix"? } or { "type": "webdav", "url" } copies each one there too, keeping as many; its credentials are set in the apps (Settings, Backups) or NUDGE_BACKUP_REMOTE_USER and NUDGE_BACKUP_REMOTE_SECRET, never here.
